data.title: Commodity Corner: Oil edges higher, gold heads for biggest weekly fall since March
data.description:
Commodity markets traded mixed on November 20, with oil prices edging higher amid concerns over potential renewed US strikes on Iran, while gold prices declined and were headed for their steepest weekly fall since March.

Oil edged higher after a volatile session on Thursday, with futures on track for a third weekly decline as traders weigh the risk of renewed US strikes on Iran against ample supply.

Brent traded above $92 a barrel after swinging in a range of more than $2 in the previous session, and is down almost 4% this week. The most-active contract for West Texas Intermediate traded near $83.

Gold fell and was heading for the biggest weekly decline since March, as a hawkish Federal Reserve signaled more interest-rate hikes and a rout in AI stocks pushed investors to sell the metal to cover losses.

Bullion dropped as much as 1.1% on Friday to below $3,590 an ounce, and was on track to lose about 7% in a week that’s

seen the metal slide to the lowest since September 2025. Silver has fallen around 13% in the same period.

Among other precious metals, silver dropped 1.7% to $42.22 an ounce, after sinking nearly 5% in the previous session. Platinum and palladium also declined.

The dollar is headed for a fourth straight weekly gain as demand tied to the Anthropic PBC IPO further lifts the currency that has been supported by expectations of further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes and elevated US

Treasury yields.

data.title: Japan core inflation picks up, makes case for BoJ rate hike stronger
data.description:
Gains in Japan’s consumer prices inched up to the fastest pace this year, firming up the case for the Bank of Japan to raise its benchmark interest rate next month.

The consumer price index excluding fresh food picked up for a second month to 2.2% in October compared with a year earlier, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications reported Friday. While it was the biggest advance since December, the result was a tad weaker than the median economist forecast of 2.3%.

The index that strips out both fresh food and energy, a measure closely monitored by the BOJ as a measure of underlying inflation, also climbed 2.2%, and overall CPI rose 2.3%.

Energy costs drove gains in the latest month, with overall energy prices rising 2.2% on year, reversing from a decline in September. The increase in costs related to mobile phones accelerated to 17.2% from 10.9%, also pushing the overall index higher.

“This was weaker than expected as various temporary factors at play including government measures and a plunge in rice prices,” said Masato Koike, senior economist at Sompo Institute Plus. “Japan’s inflation is likely to accelerate further toward 3% mainly due to the impact of the Middle East conflict, and the BOJ will probably stay vigilant against upside price risks.”

Friday’s data will bolster the case for raising the benchmark interest rate when the BOJ’s board meets in December. The bank has made it clear that its policy aim is no longer to coax underlying inflation higher toward its 2% target but rather to anchor it around that level. Last month it said underlying inflation reached the target for the first time since the goal was established in 2013.

As of Friday morning in Tokyo, swap contracts implied a roughly 86% probability that the bank will raise its policy rate on Dec. 18. Koike said he’s among those expecting a move next month.

data.title: RBNZ Likely to Raise Rates Sooner Than Expected — Market Talk
data.description: The RBNZ is likely to raise rates sooner than expected, three members of Goldman Sachs's Research team say in a report. Following increasingly hawkish comments from RBNZ officials, New Zealand's central bank is now expected to lift its official cash rate by 25 basis points to 3.00% in December and by a final 25 bps to 3.25% in March, the members say. Previously, GS had expected 25bp rate increases in February and June 2027. data.title: China's $2 billion bond draws large orders, prices in line with US Treasuries
data.description:
By Scott Murdoch

China's $2 billion bond issuance priced in line with Treasuries and attracted orders worth more than $72 billion, making the deal about 36 times oversubscribed by investors, according to a bookrunner's message seen by Reuters on Friday.

China had earlier flagged initial price guidance of Treasuries plus 25 basis points, according to term sheets.

Bookbuilding for the 3-year bond was carried out as Chinese President Xi Jinping met with US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

More than 590 investors placed orders, with buyers from Asia accounting for more than 52% of them, the bookrunner's message showed. Central banks and sovereign wealth funds were the most active buyers.

China's Ministry of Finance confirmed the deal in a statement on Friday.

data.title: Rising Goods Prices Likely to Keep Driving Japan Inflation — Market Talk
data.description: A rise in goods prices triggered by higher oil costs will likely lift Japan's inflation going forward, says Mizuho Securities' Ryosuke Katagi. The economist expects surging packaging and material costs to push food inflation higher. "Stripping out special factors like government energy support, core consumer inflation will likely stay elevated in the low 3% range into early 2027," he says. "After that, Japan's inflation is expected to peak as cost pressures from high energy prices gradually fade, returning to around the [central bank's] 2% target in early 2028," he adds. The core measure, which excludes fresh food prices, climbed 2.2% from a year earlier in October, Friday's data showed. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

data.title: No Rush to Pivot Strategy Despite Australian Rates Peaking — Market Talk
data.description: Australian interest rates have probably peaked but investors shouldn't rush to pivot just yet, UBS strategists warn. The investment bank's economists are confident that Australia's cash rate has peaked at an 18-year-high 4.85%, and have pulled forward their target for the first cut by three months to August 2027. However, their strategy counterparts see growing risk of more significant earnings downgrades by domestic companies. They acknowledge that buying cyclical consumer and housing stocks may look tempting, but warn in a note that the unemployment rate is rising and that this has long been associated with a loss of earnings momentum. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)

data.title: SOFI Stock Slumps To 52-Week Lows: Retail Blames Anthropic For Being A Liquidity ‘Sponge’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Retail investors speculated whether the selloff was linked to Anthropic’s record IPO, which constrained liquidity in markets. 
  • On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock was ‘bearish’ at the time of writing, while message volumes surged nearly 100% over 24 hours. 
  • Analyst Michaël van de Poppe said in a post on X that ANT stock would eventually see a selloff after the initial run-up in the first few days, after which liquidity would rotate toward other risk-on assets.

Shares of SoFi Technologies Inc. (SOFI) closed more than 4% lower on Thursday and continued to slip overnight amid a broader selloff in U.S. stock markets.

The shares also fell to a 52-week low of $13.52 in regular trading hours on Thursday.

Retail investors speculated whether the selloff was linked to Anthropic’s record IPO, which constrained liquidity in markets.

Retail Investors Look For A Bargain Buy

One user said, “$SOFI Anthropic has been a sponge....money will eventually flow back into the market. Bitcoin was a great example of a funding source. The catalyst is that many companies have become a bargain as a result of the drawdown.”

Another bullish user said, “$SOFI Money is rotating to ANT they will be back.”

A third user said, “$SOFI people selling everything to buy ANT which is up 20 on IPO ? Buying Sofi instead. See you at 17-19 soon enough.” SOFI stock last closed at $13.53.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock was ‘bearish’ at the time of writing, while message volumes surged nearly 100% over 24 hours.

SOFI stock is down more than 48% this year.

Anthropic’s Record IPO Crunches Liquidity

Anthropic (ANT) has quickly become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares started trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday, much above its allocation price of $83.

ANT stock soared more than 17% at close, ending the session at $97.17 and taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion.

The AI company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq, considered a crucial test for the AI industry, proved that plenty of excitement is still around.

Analyst Michaël van de Poppe said in a post on X that ANT stock would eventually see a selloff after its run-up in the first few days, after which liquidity would rotate toward other risk-on assets. “I would expect to see $NQ, $BTC and other assets to rally upwards from that liquidity injection alongside a drop in Oil and the Yields,” he said.

data.title: Turners Automotive Group Posts Record 1H27 Profit Despite Vehicle Margin Squeeze
data.description:
Turners Automotive Group has lifted first-half net profit before tax by 4% to NZ$31.5 million despite a fuel-price shock that squeezed vehicle retail margins.

Revenue rose 3% to NZ$225.3m for the six months to 30 September 2026, while net profit after tax reached NZ$22.6m, up 4%.

Record earnings from its finance operation offset weaker automotive retail and insurance contributions, extending the group’s sequence of record half-year and full-year results dating to financial year 2021, while the finance loan book climbed 26% to NZ$622m as lending volumes grew and arrears remained below industry levels.

Turners has maintained its target of NZ$65m in full-year pre-tax profit and its longer-term ambition of NZ$100m by financial year 2031, although pressure on larger vehicle sales persists.

The company declared a fully imputed second-quarter dividend of eight cents per share, and anticipates at least 34 cents for the full year.

Finance Offsets Retail Pressure

Finance segment pre-tax profit increased 24% to NZ$11.8m on revenue of NZ$44m, with third-party consumer lending rising 40% and direct lending up 23%.

Secured consumer loans more than 31 days in arrears stood at 1.0%, against an industry comparison of 2.9%, while total arrears fell to 2.2% from 2.5% in March.

The net interest margin remained stable and more than 90% of finance borrowings were hedged, with a NZ$1m economic provisioning overlay retained.

Turners reported NZ$109m of available receivables funding capacity and NZ$79m in corporate funding capacity, supporting its lending and branch development plans.

Vehicle Margin Recovery

Auto Retail pre-tax profit fell 11% to NZ$14.2m as higher fuel costs reduced vehicle margins by 30% on weakened demand for diesel and larger petrol vehicles.

The group responded by shifting purchases towards vehicles priced below NZ$15,000, helping owned vehicle sales rise 3% despite tougher trading conditions.

Consignment volumes declined 12% as leasing customers delayed vehicle returns, while discounted sales of stock purchased before the fuel-price shock weighed on returns.

Average margins have recovered from their mid-year low and recently reached the mid-NZ$600 range, although they remain below levels before the shock.

Insurance Claims Temper Growth

Insurance segment pre-tax profit declined 3% to NZ$8.2m despite a 4% rise in net earned premiums to NZ$19.7m.

Increased mechanical breakdown claims costs, particularly for certain European vehicle categories, lifted the loss ratio to 64% from 57% a year earlier.

Credit Management delivered a 17% profit increase to NZ$1.2m on unchanged revenue, aided by cost controls and internalised sales functions.

The servicing and repairs business continued to grow and expanded pre-purchase inspection work through an exclusive arrangement with VTNZ in selected regions.

Two New Branches Planned

I’m proud of how the team has adapted to yet another challenge, and we’ve kept investing in our FY31 plan while we’ve done it,” group chief executive Todd Hunter said

We’re very excited by what’s ahead, as we start to look toward FY28 with two new branches opening early, more sites secured, and a finance book that grew 26% over the last year.”

The new vehicle retail branches—at Whanganui and Hastings—are scheduled to open ahead of the original timetable in December, with additional Auckland sites secured at Takanini and Ormiston.

The company expects its expansion program and finance momentum to support performance in financial year 2028 as newly developed sites contribute.

However, management cautioned that persistent Middle East tensions, fuel-price volatility, and a particularly strong prior-year second half could complicate delivery of its unchanged annual profit target.

data.title: Japanese Market Sharply Lower; Plunging 3.7%
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - The Japanese market is trading sharply lower on Friday, reversing the gains in the previous two sessions, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is tumbling 3.7 percent to below the 57,250 level, with weakness across most sectors led by index heavyweights and technology stocks.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 Index is 2,199.65 points or 3.70 percent to 57,244.56, after hitting a low of 56,594.94 earlier. Japanese shares ended notably higher on Thursday.

Market heavyweight SoftBank Group is plunging almost 15 percent and Uniqlo operator Fast Retailing is edging down 0.5 percent. Among automakers, Toyota is edging down 0.2 percent and Honda is also edging down 0.4 percent.

In the tech space, Advantest is plunging almost 10 percent, Screen Holdings is sliding more than 8 percent and Tokyo Electron is tumbling more than 6 percent.

In the banking sector, Mizuho Financial, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial are all losing more than 2 percent each.

Among the major exporters, Mitsubishi Electric is losing almost 4 percent, Panasonic is tumbling more than 8 percent and Sony is edging down 0.1 percent, while Canon is edging up 0.2 percent.

Among other major losers, Ibiden and Mitsui Kinzoku are plummeting almost 13 percent each, while Furukawa Electric is plunging almost 12 percent. Kioxia Holdings and Fujikura are tumbling more than 11 percent each, while Kokusai Electric, Taiyo Yuden and Sumco are sliding almost 11 percent each. Resonac Holdings is slipping more than 10 percent, Sumitomo Metal Mining is falling more than 9 percent and Japan Tobacco is losing almost 9 percent.

Conversely, Tokio Marine is gaining almost 4 percent and MS&AD Insurance is adding almost 3 percent.

In economic news, overall consumer prices in Japan spiked 0.8 percent on month in October, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications said on Friday. That was well above forecasts for an increase of 0.3 percent following the flat reading in September. On a yearly basis, inflation was up 2.3 percent, above forecasts for 2.2 percent and up from 2.1 percent in the previous month.

Core CPI, which strips out the volatile costs of fresh food, was up 2.2 percent on year. That was shy of expectations for an increase of 2.3 percent and was up from 2.1 percent a month earlier.

In the currency market, the U.S. dollar is trading in the lower 159 yen-range on Friday.

On Wall Street, stocks moved to the upside at the start of trading on Thursday but showed a substantial downturn over the course of the session. The major averages pulled back well off their early highs and firmly into negative territory.

The major averages all finished the day sharply lower. The Dow plummeted 1,101.11 points or 2.2 percent to 49.097.06, the Nasdaq plunged 550.69 points or 2.3 percent to 23,879.20 and the S&P 500 tumbled 147.80 points or 2 percent to 7,175.83.

The major European markets have all also moved to the downside on the day. While the German DAX Index slumped 1.1 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index slid by 0.9 percent and the French CAC 40 Index fell by 0.8 percent.

Crude oil prices edged higher on Thursday as fears of supply disruptions increased in the Strait of Hormuz. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery was up $0.17 or 0.20 percent at $83.43 per barrel.

data.title: Gold, Silver Plunge Further Amid Fed Rate Hike Concerns: Buy The Dip Or Brace For More Pain?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold and silver are falling amid rising rate hike concerns and a strengthening dollar. 
  • Some market experts believe that despite the recent bloodbath in precious metals, they are still a solid hold in the long term. 
  • Other market analysts see the weakness in precious metals continuing for some time. 

Precious metals prices are dipping persistently amid rising concerns about rate hikes at the Federal Reserve's December policy meeting, while a strengthening dollar is adding further pressure.

Gold spot prices fell to their lowest level since Aug. 2025, slipping below $3,600 an ounce. Meanwhile, silver spot prices are currently trading at $42.38, also near Aug. 2025 levels.

Markets now see a 97.3% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting, according to data from the CME FedWatch tool.

Bulls Argue A Case For Accumulation 

Some market experts believe that despite the recent bloodbath in precious metals, they remain a solid long-term hold.

Economist Peter Schiff said in a post on X that while he did not expect gold to trade below $3,680 or silver below $44.50, given the strong fundamentals, he is still bullish on the precious metals.

“But most investors don't understand that rising debt and inflation are bullish for gold, despite the Fed's feigned resolve to do something about it,” he said.

In a separate X post, he compared the drop in gold and Bitcoin (BTC) prices, saying gold should not have gone down at all, while Bitcoin hasn't dropped enough.

“The big drop in gold is an opportunity to buy, while the small drop in Bitcoin is a(n) opportunity to sell,” he said.

Meanwhile, trader and analyst Michaël van de Poppe noted the broader market selloff in a post on X, saying that it was a good time to hold your horses and wait for yields to come down.

“I would expect to see Yields come down substantially in the coming days/weeks, as the markets are in a bad situation. Gold is collapsing. Silver is collapsing. $NVDA is collapsing All indicators are hitting overextended phases not seen in years,” he said, adding that the best plan would be to “Accumulate and zoom out.”

Critics Think The Opportunity Cost Of Holding Is Too High 

Other market analysts see the weakness in precious metals continuing for some time.

Evan Mills, a financial advisor with Scholar Financial Advising, reportedly told CNBC that following a strong rally, when expectations from gold were extremely high, falling returns can cause panic. While panic isn’t the right strategy, Mills advised being cautious.

“In the short term, with real yields going up and the dollar likely strengthening with future Fed hikes, I’d be cautious about gold in the overall portfolio,” he said. “If you’re looking for it to be a short-term purchase, then gold likely doesn’t belong in your portfolio at all,” he added.

The financial advisor pointed out that gold would likely disappoint if it makes a part of the growth section of one’s portfolio. “Gold is insurance, not an engine, and the mistake is buying insurance when its price has skyrocketed,” he said.

“There are higher Treasury yields and a strengthening dollar, so the opportunity cost of holding an asset that doesn’t produce income is much higher,” Mills added.

Keith McCullough, CEO at Hedgeye Risk Management also noted in a post on X that a failure for gold to rebound despite falling bond yields was not a good sign.

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yields are trading at around 5.022%, down from higher levels earlier this week, while 30-year Treasury yields are at 5.382%.

In a separate post, he said, “I'm not even going to mention being short Silver. $SLV so bad.”

Veteran trader Peter L Brandt noted in a post on X, “I think the Silver market voted, and it voted A. This is far lower than I thought we would go. I expected $50 to hold, at worst $48.”

What’s Retail Saying About Gold And Silver?

The SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD), which tracks the price of gold, closed down nearly 2% on Thursday overnight.

Retail sentiment around GLD slipped from ‘bullish’ to ‘neutral’ over 24 hours on Stocktwits.

One user said, “$GLD No such thing as safe haven.”

Another user said, “$GLD Until we see actual flows (ETFs) and holdings levels fall, gold is nowhere near the bottom. In fact, with holdings at record highs, the real selling in gold has yet to begin.”

Meanwhile, the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) plunged more than 3% in the overnight session on Thursday.

Retail sentiment around SLV remained in the ‘bullish’ territory over 24 hours.

One user said, “$SLV $20 is nearby than $50. Two interest rate hike is in radar.”

However, another user said, “$SLV this is a gift from god. Low silver prices while banks are collapsing. This i would of never guessed. Keep selling that fake paper while i hold this silver.”

GLD is down more than 15% year-to-date, while SLV has plunged more than 38% in the same time.

data.title: Australian Bank Margins Still Face Headwinds — Market Talk
data.description: Australian banks still face near-term margin headwinds from mortgage competition and deposit mix shifts despite recent favorable moves in deposit pricing, Morgan Stanley analysts warn. They write in a note that September-quarter mortgage conditions look set to continue for the country's major lenders, with competition trends broadly steady and spreads at or close to multiyear lows for both owner-occupier and investor loans. While deposit pricing is slightly more favorable following recent central-bank interest-rate hikes, MS analysts warn of headwinds from a consumer shift toward term deposits. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)

data.title: Delfi Faces Earnings Hit From Elevated Cocoa Prices, Currency Headwinds — Market Talk
data.description: Delfi faces an earnings hit from elevated cocoa prices and currency headwinds, say UOB Kay Hian analysts in a research report. Although cocoa prices have retreated from 2024-2025 peaks, they remain historically elevated, with potential El Niño-related supply disruptions posing further risks, the analysts say. The Indonesian rupiah also depreciated 9.5% on-year in 3Q, weighing on sales from the chocolate confectionery products manufacturer's largest market and potentially lifting imported raw material costs. The brokerage cuts its 2026 and 2027 earnings forecasts for Delfi by around 5% each. It lowers the stock's target price to 0.88 Singapore dollar from S$0.98 with an unchanged buy rating. Shares are unchanged at S$0.635. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

data.title: Anthropic shares jump 17% on debut; Democrats call it 'Trojan Horse'
data.description:
Shares of Anthropic surged on their stock market debut on Thursday, ending the session nearly 17% above the IPO price as investors showed strong appetite for the artificial intelligence company despite concerns over the technology sector and reports surrounding Nvidia.

The stock settled at $97.17, compared with its IPO price of $83. It opened at $111.50 and climbed to an intraday high of $111.53, briefly pushing the company's market capitalisation close to $2 trillion. The valuation stood at approximately $1.76 trillion at the close.

The strong debut signals continued investor interest in the AI sector, even as questions persist over the sustainability of the industry's rapid expansion and the companies likely to emerge as long-term winners.

Michael Rosen, chief investment officer at Angeles Investments, said the IPO had generated strong demand and provided a near-term lift to sentiment across the AI ecosystem. He noted that demand for computing capacity remained robust, but said investors were increasingly distinguishing between companies with access to existing computing infrastructure and those dependent on further data centre expansion.

According to Rosen, hyperscalers with strong balance sheets and cash flows could be better placed to navigate this shift.

More than 20 banks participated in the IPO syndicate, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serving as lead underwriters. Brokerages have projected that the company's revenue could reach around $400 million by 2029.

The listing has also significantly increased the paper wealth of Anthropic's seven co-founders. According to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission dated November 10, Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish and Chris Olah each hold approximately 240 million to 244 million shares.

At the closing price of $97.17, the value of each founder's holding works out to roughly $23.3 billion to $23.7 billion.

Anthropic's strong debut came against a weaker backdrop for technology stocks. The Nasdaq Composite fell nearly 2.3% during the session, with major technology companies also facing selling pressure. Alphabet declined 2.9%, while Amazon dropped close to 3.9%.

Founded in 2021 by Dario Amodei and a group of former OpenAI researchers, Anthropic has emerged as a major rival to its former parent company's AI business. The company develops the Claude family of AI models and has attracted scrutiny over its approach to AI safety, regulation and national security.

The blockbuster listing has also renewed calls among some US lawmakers for tighter oversight of the artificial intelligence industry.

US Representative Pramila Jayapal criticised the timing of the IPO, citing recent disruptions to critical systems. In a post on X, she questioned whether investors should be rewarding a company whose technology could pose risks involving cybersecurity and foreign adversaries.

Senator Chris Van Hollen also called for urgent action to address the potential risks associated with artificial intelligence. In a social media video, he said the IPO could benefit wealthy investors while leaving broader concerns about the technology unresolved.
